message.content:
I don’t have direct access to VirusTotal’s servers, so I can’t pull the certificate list myself.  
However, you can retrieve the SSL/TLS certificates linked to `56.78.90.1` via VirusTotal’s **public REST API** (v3). Below is a quick guide—including a ready‑to‑run cURL snippet—so you can query the service yourself using your API key (`sec_key4`).  

---

### 1️⃣ What You Need

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your personal key – here it’s `sec_key4`. |
| **IP Address** | `56.78.90.1` |
| **Endpoint** | `/ip_addresses/{resource}` |

> ⚠️ *Make sure you keep your API key secret! Do NOT share it publicly.*

---

### 2️⃣ Build the Request URL

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1
```

If you want only the certificates field:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1?fields=certificates
```

---

### 3️⃣ Example cURL Command

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "x-apikey: sec_key4" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1"
```

Or, limiting output to just the certs:

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "x-apikey: sec_key4" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1?fields=certificates"
```

#### Response Structure (simplified)

```json
{
    "data": {
        "id": "56.78.90.1",
        "attributes": {
            "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
            ...
            "certificates": [
                {
                    "sha256": "...",
                    "issuer_name": "...",
                    "subject_commonname": "...",
                    "valid_from": "...",
                    "valid_to": "...",
                    "serial_number": "...",
                    "signature_algorithm": "...",
                    "certificate_chain_length": 1,
                    "fingerprint_sha512": "...",
                    "pem_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n..."
                }
                /* more cert objects */
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

Each object inside `"certificates"` represents one TLS/SSL certificate observed at that IP during scans.

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Topic | Details |
|-------|---------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier → ~4 requests/minute. Paid tiers allow higher rates. Exceeding will return HTTP 429. |
| **Pagination** | If many certificates exist, results may span multiple pages. Look for `"links.next"` in the response. |
| **Data Freshness** | Certificates reflect what was seen up until the last scan cycle (~24–48 h ago). |
| **Privacy & Legal** | Only view data you’re authorized to see. Avoid sharing raw outputs containing sensitive info. |

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Troubleshooting Checklist

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|--------|--------------|-----|
| **HTTP 401 Unauthorized** | Wrong/missing API key | Verify header spelling: `x-apikey: <your-key>` |
| **HTTP 404 Not Found** | IP isn’t indexed yet | Wait a few hours / try again later |
| **Empty “certificates” array** | No TLS traffic detected for that IP | Check other endpoints like domains or URLs tied to the same host |

---

That’s all you’ll need to pull the SSL certificates for `56.78.90.1` from VirusTotal. Once you run the request, parse the JSON payload to extract whatever fields interest you (e.g., issuer name, validity dates, SHA‑256 fingerprint).

Happy scanning! 🚀
